chapter_title: Concerning the Fasting of the Saints
chapter_note: This chapter is dominated by late institutional/pastoral instruction on fasting (including weekly practice and alms), wrapped in a standard dialogue opening. Two paragraphs preserve older doctrinal kernels in a more impersonal, process-oriented voice: the mechanics of purification of the soul/light in relation to food and the undefiled condition of the Children of Light. The numbered 'four works' structure appears to be an editorial pastoral organization into which these kernels were fitted.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Formulaic dialogue attribution (“Once more the enlightener speaks…”) is a hagiographic/compilation frame marker.
Institutional topic-setting about saints’ fasting and its usefulness; no cosmological mechanism, written as practical doctrinal instruction.
Ascetic/disciplinary rationale (“punish his body by fasting… subdues…”) in a prescriptive conditional aimed at practitioners; not cosmos→cosmos mapping.

paragraphs.core_text: This soul that comes into him in the administration of his food, day by day; it shall be made holy, cleansed, purified, and washed from the adulteration of the darkness that is mixed in with it.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the pastoral list label “The second:” which embeds an older doctrinal mechanism inside an editorial ‘four works of fasting’ scheme.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The extracted sentence is mechanistic and impersonal (purification/mixture language tied to food), reflecting Manichaean cosmological soteriology rather than institutional instruction.

paragraphs.core_text: the mystery of [the children] of light in whom there is neither corruption nor [...] the food, nor wound it. Rather, they are holy, [there is nothing] in them that defiles, as they live in peace.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the pastoral/exhortative lead-in and list label: “The third: That person shall make every deed a holy one;” which shifts from describing a state to prescribing behavior.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Core fragment describes an undefiled ontological condition (“children of light… nothing… that defiles”) rather than instructing an audience; the paragraph’s opening is a later applicatory pivot.
Ethical/practice instruction (“restrain their hands…”) embedded in fasting discourse; likely institutional discipline (cf. ‘seals’ praxis) despite cosmological terms like “Cross” and “living soul.”
Generalizing exhortation to persist daily and to make the body’s members fast; explicit practice-focus and community discipline voice.
Institutional accommodation (“lord’s day”) plus alms as participation; clearly later community practice rather than substrate cosmology.
